title: Vec, the growable list
summary: vec! builds, push grows (needs mut), for walks the elements.
lecture: `Vec<T>` is the growable list. Build one with the `vec!` macro - `vec![10, 20, 30]` - or start empty with `Vec::new()`. Growing it with `push` mutates, so the binding must be `let mut`.
A plain array `[10, 20, 30]` looks similar but has a fixed size and no `push`. The types are different, and so are the errors when you mix them up.
`for n in &v` walks the elements. Iterating a borrowed vec yields references; simple arithmetic on them works thanks to auto-deref, and the iterator decks later make this precise.

example.caption: mut because push changes the vec.
